preview.headline: Flyers Host Oilers in Quick Rematch with Rest Disadvantage Equalized
preview.summary: The Edmonton Oilers travel to face the Philadelphia Flyers just days after a narrow head-to-head meeting. Both teams enter playing their second game in four days with zero days of rest, setting up a grueling battle of attrition.
preview.away_analysis: The Oilers carry a four-game winning streak despite underlying metrics that suggest considerable reliance on finishing and special teams. Ranking 28th in expected goals percentage and 29th in expected goals for per 60, Edmonton struggles to control five-on-five play. However, their elite power play, operating at 32.86 percent for third in the league, consistently bails them out.
preview.home_analysis: The Flyers dominate the territorial battle at five-on-five, ranking 7th in expected goals percentage and 6th in high-danger chances percentage. Philadelphia's defense suppresses chances efficiently, ranking 3rd in expected goals against per 60. Despite this strong chance creation, a 24th-ranked power play prevents them from converting territorial dominance into consistent wins.
matchup_edges: Philadelphia holds a massive five-on-five advantage in expected goals and high-danger chance generation.
Edmonton possesses a lethal power play ranking 3rd in the league compared to Philadelphia's 24th-ranked unit.
The Flyers suppress scoring chances brilliantly, ranking 3rd in expected goals against per 60.
preview.x_factor: Special teams execution will dictate the flow, as Edmonton's elite power play matches up against Philadelphia's disciplined and solid penalty kill.
preview.key_question: Can the Flyers translate their five-on-five territorial dominance into goals against an Oilers team riding high on a four-game win streak?
preview.quick_takeaway: Philadelphia controls play better at five-on-five, but Edmonton's dangerous power play makes them a constant threat to steal a win on zero rest.

preview.headline: Flames and Ducks Battle in Tired Pacific Division Rematch
preview.summary: The Calgary Flames visit the Anaheim Ducks for a quick turnaround meeting, with both clubs playing their second game in four days and carrying zero days of rest.
preview.away_analysis: The Flames enter with sub-50% underlying metrics across the board, ranking 20th in expected goals percentage and 22nd in Corsi For. Their offense struggles to generate sustained pressure at 5-on-5, sitting 24th in expected goals for per 60 and 29th in shooting percentage at 7.61%. Fortunately, special teams provide a massive lift, anchored by a lethal power play ranked 4th in the league and a solid penalty kill.
preview.home_analysis: The Ducks hold a slight edge in possession control, ranking 14th in Corsi For %, but struggle heavily to suppress high-danger chances, sitting 30th in high-danger chance share and 31st in expected goals against per 60. While their shooting percentage is a healthy 9th overall, their underlying expected goals percentage sits down at 27th. They feature a powerhouse power play ranking 1st in the league, though it is counterbalanced by a vulnerable penalty kill ranking 22nd.
matchup_edges: Calgary boasts a notable advantage on special teams discipline and penalty kill efficiency.
Anaheim holds the upper hand in 5-on-5 shot attempt generation, ranking 14th in Corsi For %.
The Flames possess superior defensive chance suppression, ranking 14th in expected goals against per 60 compared to the Ducks at 31st.
preview.x_factor: Special teams efficiency will be pivotal, as both squads feature elite power plays going up against penalty kills of varying reliability.
preview.key_question: Can the Ducks protect their porous defense against a Flames team desperate for more even-strength offense?
preview.quick_takeaway: Both tired teams enter on identical schedules, making special teams execution and defensive zone composure the deciding factors in this Pacific Division clash.

preview.headline: Panthers Visit Stars in Battle of Exhausted Contenders
preview.summary: The Florida Panthers wrap up a busy stretch to face a Dallas Stars squad that excels in chance suppression and elite expected goal control despite matching zero days of rest.
preview.away_analysis: Despite riding a three-game win streak, the Panthers are playing their fourth game in seven days with zero days of rest. Florida brings a disciplined style that ranks 3rd in Corsi Against per 60 and 7th in expected goals against, backed by a strong 7th-ranked penalty kill. However, their 25th-ranked expected goals for per 60 highlights an offense that struggles to generate consistent pressure.
preview.home_analysis: The Stars enter this matchup dominating the underlying metrics, claiming 2nd in expected goals percentage and 4th in high-danger chance share. Dallas boasts the league's top-ranked expected goals against per 60 and an elite 2nd-ranked penalty kill. Like Florida, they are playing on the second half of a back-to-back with zero days of rest, testing their structural depth.
matchup_edges: Dallas holds a massive edge in expected goal share, ranking 2nd overall compared to Florida at 16th.
The Stars defensive suppression is elite, ranking 1st in expected goals against per 60.
Both teams feature top-tier penalty kills, with Dallas ranking 2nd and Florida ranking 7th.
preview.x_factor: Fatigue management on zero days of rest for both squads, particularly with Florida playing their fourth game in a week.
preview.key_question: Can Dallas convert their dominant expected goal share into actual goals against a stingy Florida defensive structure?
preview.quick_takeaway: Dallas controls the territorial play with elite underlying metrics, but both teams face heavy fatigue playing on zero days of rest.

preview.headline: Golden Knights Host Struggling Canucks Looking to Reverse Skid
preview.summary: The Vancouver Canucks visit the Vegas Golden Knights on November 15, 2026, looking to snap a brutal seven-game losing streak. Vegas took the first meeting of the season 3-2 on October 4 and enters with the clear statistical advantage across possession, expected goals, and special teams.
preview.away_analysis: The Canucks are mired in a seven-game slide and rank near the bottom of the league across nearly every core metric, including 31st in Corsi For% at 45.92 and 32nd in high-danger chance share at 38.7%. Their special teams present a glaring vulnerability, anchored by a league-worst 62.69% penalty kill that leaves them highly susceptible to opponent power plays.
preview.home_analysis: Vegas holds a distinct edge in underlying play, ranking 14th in expected goals percentage at 50.95% and carrying a solid 51.64% high-danger chance share. While their shooting percentage sits low at 26th overall, their top-tier power play clicking at 27.42% provides an optimal avenue to exploit Vancouver's abysmal penalty kill.
matchup_edges: Vegas owns a massive special teams advantage with the league's 5th-ranked power play facing Vancouver's 32nd-ranked penalty kill.
The Golden Knights control play better at 5-on-5, holding the 14th-ranked expected goals share compared to the Canucks' 31st-ranked mark.
Vegas generates a higher volume of quality looks, ranking 13th in high-danger chance share against a Canucks side sitting dead last.
preview.x_factor: Vancouver's league-worst penalty kill facing off against Vegas's lethal top-five power play.
preview.key_question: Can the Canucks find any defensive stability to snap their seven-game losing streak, or will the Golden Knights exploit their glaring special teams mismatch?
preview.quick_takeaway: Vegas enters with decisive advantages in play-driving metrics and special teams against a reeling Canucks squad desperate for answers.

preview.headline: Predators Look to Extend Streak Against Tired Sharks
preview.summary: The Nashville Predators bring a sizzling seven-game winning streak into San Jose to face a Sharks squad playing on zero days of rest. While the Predators have run hot on special teams and goaltending, the Sharks are searching for traction amid poor underlying possession and defensive metrics.
preview.away_analysis: The Predators arrive riding a dominant seven-game winning streak, fueled by elite special teams and stellar goaltending. Juuse Saros ranks third in GSAx over his last 20 games, anchoring a penalty kill that sits first in the NHL at 89.66%. Although Nashville's underlying possession numbers are modest—ranking 29th in Corsi For %—they boast a top-10 actual goal share and a lethal power play ranking seventh.
preview.home_analysis: The Sharks are fighting an uphill battle with a 41.67% goals-for rate and an expected goals percentage that ranks 30th overall. San Jose struggles heavily to suppress chances, allowing a league-worst 3.41 expected goals against per 60 minutes while taking penalties at a high rate. Compounding these issues, they enter this contest on the second half of a back-to-back with zero days of rest.
matchup_edges: Nashville owns a massive special teams advantage, featuring the league's top-ranked penalty kill against a San Jose unit struggling at 21st.
Juuse Saros provides a significant edge in net over the Sharks, ranking third in recent GSAx compared to Nedeljkovic at 13th.
Schedule fatigue heavily favors the rested Predators against a San Jose team playing their second game in as many days.
preview.x_factor: San Jose's discipline and penalty trouble will be heavily tested against Nashville's seventh-ranked power play, especially given the Sharks' heavy workload on zero days of rest.
preview.key_question: Can the Sharks overcome severe fatigue and porous defensive metrics to snap Nashville's seven-game win streak?
preview.quick_takeaway: Nashville brings elite special teams and a rested roster into San Jose against a fatigued Sharks team struggling heavily with defensive suppression.
